title: Phase-gating operational runbook and sign-off flow for API/Console/Runtime release train
creator: Ava Reynolds
description: Goal: Define a phase-gated, operational runbook and sign-off flow that consolidates milestone decision criteria across API, Console, and Runtime teams so we can ship release-train-2025.3 with predictable rollouts and a single source of truth for go/no-go decisions. Scope: milestone definitions, scope-lock rules, quantitative cut criteria, stakeholder signoff flow (PM, Eng, Design, Sec, SRE, Legal), release notes coordination template, and communications choreography for canary and wide rollouts. Out of scope: per-model kernel tuning playbooks (handled by Eng runtime subteam) and marketing creative assets.
acceptance_criteria: A single runbook page published in Confluence that lists phase gates, decision owners, and required artifacts for each gate
Cut criteria defined with numeric thresholds (SLOs, error rates, perf regression limits) for the alpha->beta->general gates
Signoff checklist implemented as a shared Google sheet with explicit owner columns and time-boxed approval windows
Release notes template agreed and assigned; owners for API docs, Console UX notes, and Runtime ops notes identified
Stakeholder simulation (table-top) executed with SRE and Support; at least one simulated rollback run executed successfully
tasks: Draft gate taxonomy and decision rubric (PM lead)
Collect SLO baselines and variance tolerances from Observability (Eng/SRE)
Define scope-lock alleys: features allowed for hotfix, allowed regressions, and backout paths
Create signoff sheet and assign approvers per gate
Write release notes ownership matrix and provide templates to docs and design
Schedule table-top rollback simulation and invite cross-functional participants
Publish runbook and announce comms plan to stakeholders
milestones: 2025-08-26: Signoff sheet live and approvers assigned
2025-08-30: Release notes owners confirmed and templates circulated
2025-09-10: Scope lock (no new feature merges to release train main)
2025-09-12: Final signoff window and ship readiness check
cut_criteria: Severity-1 customer-facing errors >= 1 in last 24h for canary => block
Increase in 95th-percentile tail latency > 20% against baseline for API routes tagged as critical => block
End-to-end regression in console flows measured by functional smoke tests failing > 2 tests => block
Unresolved security findings marked critical by Security => block
Telemetry pipeline gaps preventing reliable SLO measurement => conditional stop until mitigated
comms_plan: Primary channels: #release-train (Slack), product-release@redwood.com (email), confluence runbook page. Template messages for: pre-freeze announcement, signoff reminder (24h and 2h), canary start/stop, rollback initiation. Ops will own the canary start message; PM will own the final ship announcement. Use the release notes checklist in the shared sheet to populate the release email. Postmortem cadence: 48h incident review if any block occurred during ship window.
rollout_strategy: Progressive canary by customer tier/region: 1) internal dogfood, 2) 0.5% traffic external canary (non-critical customers), 3) 5% traffic, 4) 25% traffic, 5) 100%. Automations: traffic ramp automated via feature flag service with manual abort. Fallback: immediate traffic cutoff + diversion to previous model bundle in the runtime pool. For Dedicated customers, use capacity isolation and manual opt-in for the first 24h.
release_notes_coordination: Owners: PM: Ava Reynolds (overall), Docs: Lina O'Connor (API docs), Design: Jorge Mendes (Console UX highlights), Eng Runtime: Priya Shah (ops/upgrade notes). Template includes: TL;DR, customer impact, upgrade steps, known issues, rollback instructions, telemetry check-list. All sections must be completed 48h before final signoff. PRs: GitHub repo redwood/docs: PRs must reference this ticket (PM-21346).
observability_and_launch_readiness: Dashboards to validate: API latency (p50/p95/p99), error budget burn, end-to-end console smoke tests, runtime memory/GPU utilization per model variant, KV-cache hit ratio. Pre-ship readiness: all dashboards green and alerting stable for 72h. Alerts and runbook playbooks linked in the Confluence page for on-call response.
